title: fix(rest): export lookup cells name the record by the target object's title field
body:
Fixes #24944

Clause-②: no

## What changes

`GET /api/v1/data/:object/export` (Display → Export as CSV / XLSX) wrote a lookup, master_detail, user or tree cell from the lookup field's own `displayField`. Without one, it took the first scalar key of a fixed list (`name`, `title`, `label`, `full_name`, …) found on the expanded record. It never read the target object's `nameField`. A HotCRM contact declares `nameField: 'full_name'`, has no `name` column and has a job `title` column, so it exported as its job title.

- `packages/rest/src/export-format.ts`
  - New `withReferenceTitleFields(metaMap, readSchema)`. It reads each reference target's schema once per export (deduplicated by target) and stamps `titleField` on that field's meta. It is best-effort per target and never throws: a target whose schema cannot be read keeps the key-list fallback.
  - `ExportCellMeta` is an export-only extension of core's `ExportFieldMeta` with that one key. `ExportFieldMeta` in `@objectstack/core` is not touched, and nothing new is exported from the package index.
  - `displayFromRecord` reads, in order: the lookup's own `displayField`; else the target's `titleField`; else, only when the target resolves no title, the key list; else the record id.
- `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`
  - The export route's schema read becomes one local `readObjectSchema` (the same `getMetaItem`, then `getObjectSchema`, order as before). It serves the export's own object and each target.
  - `metaMap = await withReferenceTitleFields(metaMap, readObjectSchema)` runs before the `$expand` is built.
- No key, query parameter, header, column set or payload shape moves. Only the text of a lookup cell changes, in csv, xlsx and json alike.

## The title rule: `resolveDisplayField`, not `titleFieldOf`

- `titleFieldOf` (`packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts`) is not reachable from `@objectstack/rest` without a new runtime dependency. `@objectstack/objectql` is only a devDependency here.
- `resolveDisplayField` (`@objectstack/spec/data`, `display-name.ts`) is reachable through the existing dependency. It is ADR-0079's single resolver, and plugin-audit and plugin-approvals use it to name a related record. Its rungs are `nameField`, then `displayNameField`, then a derivation. The first two rungs are exactly `titleFieldOf`'s rule. The formatter receives the resolved field and holds no rule of its own.
- On every body the protocol serves, the two answer the same. At registration the registry runs `provisionPrimary(schema, { synthesize: false })`, which is `resolveDisplayField`, and stamps the result as `nameField`. Measured through `protocol.getMetaItem` on a real engine (a throwaway probe, not committed):

  | Registered object (no pointer declared) | Served `nameField` | Old key-list pick |
  |---|---|---|
  | `id`, `subject` (text), `email` | `subject` | `email` |
  | `id`, `label` (select) | `id` | `label` (the raw option code) |
  | `title`, `full_name` (text) | `title` | `title` |
  | `amount` (number) only | none | none (id floor) |

- They differ only on a served body that carries no pointer but has a title-eligible field. There `resolveDisplayField` gives ADR-0079's derivation where `titleFieldOf` gives nothing. None of the measured registry bodies is in that state.
- Consequence: an object that declares no title is still served with a designated one. Its lookup cells now follow that designated title. In the table above, `subject` replaces `email`, and the id replaces a raw select code.

## Visible changes beyond the reported case

- **Account.** HotCRM's account declares `nameField: 'display_title'` and has a literal `name` column. Its lookup cells change from `name` to `display_title`. That follows the declaration (pinned: `Acme` becomes `Acme (EMEA)`).
- **Field-level security.** The `$expand` sub-read is the engine's own `find` on the target, so FLS deletes an unreadable title field from the expanded record. The cell then falls to the record id, not to the key list. The card's mechanism assumption 3 expected the fallback "as it does today". Today's fallback for an unreadable `full_name` is the job title, which is the defect itself. The binding ruling keeps the key list only for an object that declares neither.
- The lookup field's own `displayField` still wins (pinned as a control).

## Evidence

All readings are on `packages/rest`. They are taken at `0fb2a82b06` (the fix) and `6dabdfbeab` (the unit pins and the changeset), on top of base `693352e4c`.

- **Red on `main`.** `src/export-lookup-title-field.test.ts` run against the unmodified route: `Tests  5 failed | 2 passed (7)`. The contact cell read `[ '1', 'VP of Engineering' ]` where `[ '1', 'John Smith' ]` was expected. The two controls (the lookup's own `displayField`, and a target served with no pointer) were green.
- **Green with the fix.** The same file, now 10 tests: `Tests  10 passed (10)`.
- **Ablation 1, the title-field read.** `withReferenceTitleFields`'s `resolveDisplayField(schema as never)` was replaced by `undefined` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `6fd4e383` → `dbe37ef0`). Result: `Tests  5 failed | 2 passed (7)`, with the first pin red. Restored to `6fd4e383032f` == HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` was empty.
- **Ablation 2, the key list held back when a title exists.** `} else {` was replaced by `} {` (blob `6fd4e383` → `f6f403cc`). Result: `Tests  1 failed | 6 passed (7)`, the FLS pin. Restored hash-equal to HEAD.
- The subject is this package's own `src/`, reached by relative import, so the ablations needed no `dist/` rebuild.

## Gates

All readings below are at the final head `321ea1f2be`. That is `6dabdfbeab` with `origin/main` `6440cf1633` merged in; the merged commit touches only plugin-security and its changeset.

- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0, no findings printed.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 66 derived commands, plus the 10 families under "Declared WIDE population". All 76 were run with the exit code captured before any pipe, and all 76 exited 0.
- `--ran` reconciliation: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 66 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 66 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files  306 passed (306)`, `Tests  6154 passed | 326 skipped (6480)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **Export, then re-import, of a lookup column.** The import's reference resolver (`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`, `resolveRef`) matches a cell against `id`, the lookup's `displayField`, then `name`, `title`, `label`, `full_name`, `email` and `username`. It never reads the target's title field. Measured through `POST /api/v1/data/xt_case/import` on the fixture of this PR:
  - `John Smith` (a contact named by its formula `full_name`) answers `reference_not_found`. So do `Wren` (a stored `displayNameField` that is not on the list) and `Acme (EMEA)` (a formula `display_title`).
  - The cells `main` wrote all resolved: `VP of Engineering` and `Chief Procurement Officer` by `title`, and `Acme` by `name`.
  - So a file this export writes no longer re-imports those lookup columns. The import side is in `packages/core`, which is held off for this card. It is reported to the dispatching seat as a finding, and not fixed here.
- No other import or export path was changed.
